speaker: Captain Spotless
before: A grate lets in light from a perfect city. Beneath it stands Captain Spotless, polishing his shield with a sleeve he has already polished.
after: A grate lets in light from a perfect city. Under it a young Enforcer sergeant stands to attention in a puddle, reading his orders off a card, in the only muddy boots the regime owns.

speaker: Captain Spotless
before: 'HALT. These tunnels do not exist, so you are standing in nothing, and I cannot allow you to have found it.'
after: 'HALT, please. Sergeant Scuff, Enforcers. Captain Spotless sent me to check the service tunnels in case anyone tried to sneak into the city this way, and I'm sorry to report that someone has. It's you.'

speaker: Captain Spotless
before: The Captain sits down on a barrel and, for a moment, looks very tired. 'I remember when these tunnels were full of people,' he says.
after: Sergeant Scuff sits down on a barrel and takes off his helmet. 'My gran laid pipe down here,' he says. 'She said these tunnels used to be full of people. I put that in a report once, and the Captain had me write it again.'

speaker: Captain Spotless
before: 'All four Paths, shoulder to shoulder, and nobody measuring anybody. Go on. The grate is not locked.'
after: 'All four Paths, shoulder to shoulder, and nobody measuring anybody. I'll tell the Captain I found nothing down here, which is what he says there is. Go on. The grate isn't locked.'

speaker: (name card)
before: Enforcer Captain of the Grate
after: Sub-Inspector of Tunnels That Do Not Exist

speaker: Enforcer Sergeant Scuff
before: HALT. State your height. No: do not state it. Stand at it.
after: HALT, please. Captain Spotless says nobody is to be down here, and that includes me, so let us be quick about it.

speaker: (battle UI)
before: On his 5th turn Spotless inspects your ranks: your strongest ready unit stands to attention (exhausted) and cannot block.
after: On his 5th turn Scuff holds an inspection, just as the Captain taught him: your strongest ready unit stands to attention (exhausted) and cannot block.

speaker: (battle UI)
before: Next turn: Spotless holds an inspection (your strongest unit cannot block).
after: Next turn: Scuff holds an inspection (your strongest unit cannot block).

speaker: Enforcer Sergeant Scuff
before: INSPECTION! I want heights, I want smudges, and I want every smile at the regulation angle!
after: INSPECTION! The Captain wants heights, he wants smudges, and he wants every smile at the regulation angle!

speaker: (battle UI)
before: Near the end Spotless notices a smudge on himself: his units get -1/-0 while he polishes.
after: Near the end Scuff notices the mud on his own boots: his units get -1/-0 while he scrubs.

speaker: Enforcer Sergeant Scuff
before: A SMUDGE is TREASON! ...It's on me, isn't it.
after: Mud. On the boots. The Captain will see it from all the way up there, I know he will.

speaker: (battle UI)
before: Spotless polishes: his units get -1/-0.
after: Scuff scrubs his boots: his units get -1/-0.

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: There is glass on every side of me, and behind the glass there are faces in white coats, taking notes.
after: There are bars on every side of me, and behind the bars there are faces in white coats, taking notes.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Glass, and white coats, and 'again.' So that is where they had you, all those years.
after: Bars, and white coats, and 'again.' So that is where they had you, all those years.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: A man in white and gold, who knelt and then stood up. And before that, those rooms of yours with glass on every side.
after: A man in white and gold, who knelt and then stood up. And before that, those rooms of yours with bars on every side.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: You took my mother and father. Then you kept me behind glass for ten years, and every morning someone said 'again'. I remember that word better than I remember their faces.
after: You took my mother and father. Then you kept me behind bars for ten years, and every morning someone said 'again'. I remember that word better than I remember their faces.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: You took my mother and father. Then you kept me behind glass for ten years, and every morning someone said 'again'. I remember that word better than I remember their faces.
after: You took my mother and father. Then you kept me behind bars for ten years, and every morning someone said 'again'. I remember that word better than I remember their faces.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: And just look at the state of you. I told her I would help whoever she sent along, but I don't recall agreeing to take in a half-drowned stray who can barely stand.
after: Come closer, dearie; my eyes aren't what they were. ...Well, look at the state of you. I told her I'd help whoever she sent along, but I never agreed to take in a half-drowned stray who can barely stand.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: I still don't know what to make of you, dearie. But you need feeding a good deal more than you need questioning, so sit yourself down for a minute.
after: I still can't make you out, dearie, and that's only partly my eyes, which see as far as a pie and not much further. But you need feeding a good deal more than you need questioning, so sit yourself down.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: You've gone as pale as flour. Sit down, sit down. Something has come back to you, hasn't it?
after: Even with my eyes I can see you've gone as pale as flour. Sit down, sit down. Something has come back to you, hasn't it?

speaker: Elder Maren
before: You've earned some truth from me in return, so here is the first piece of it: I'm not only an old tortoise who bakes.
after: The way you said that... I taught the royal children at the castle once, and there was a boy who asked his questions just that way. For a moment I thought... No. That boy is ten years dead, and I'm a foolish old tortoise.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: There's a resistance in this kingdom, and I'm its contact here in {town}. A woman called Wren leads it, from a hideout inside the Capital itself.
after: You've earned some truth in return: I'm not only an old tortoise who bakes. There's a resistance in this kingdom, and I'm its contact here in {town}. A woman called Wren leads it, from a hideout inside the Capital itself.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Somebody on the square says you've a look of the old court about you. 'That's no prince,' I told them. 'That's a damp young man with good posture.' Oh, don't look so startled, dearie.
after: Somebody on the square says you've a look of the old court about you. 'With my eyes I couldn't say,' I told them, 'but I know a damp young man with good posture when one drips on my floor.' Don't look so startled, dearie.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: I know that glass, because I helped to blow it. A long time ago I founded the study of the Paths, and I did it for the best of reasons, the way people generally do.
after: I knew that throne room, dearie. I worked at the castle once, studying the Paths, and of an afternoon I taught the royal children their letters. I began that study for the best of reasons, the way people generally do.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: {villain} took my work and built a cage out of it, and the best student I ever had stayed on to run the laboratory for him. And I ran.
after: {villain} took my study and built those cells out of it. I never forged a bar of them, but every one stands on something I wrote down. The best student I ever had stayed on to run the place for him, and I ran.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: I have been hiding here ever since with my hands in pie dough, where nobody would think to ask what else those hands had made.
after: I have been hiding here ever since with my hands in pie dough, where nobody would think to ask what those hands used to write.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: {prince}. {prince} {royal_house}. I met a boy at court once, hiding behind his mother's cloak, and he asked me why tortoises carry their houses about with them.
after: {prince}. {prince} {royal_house}. I taught a boy by that name his letters. The first day he hid behind his mother's cloak, and he asked me why tortoises carry their houses about with them.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: I knew, you see. The Warden opens that tunnel for one family only, and I knew who you were the moment you walked out of it. I was too frightened to say so.
after: And you have sat at my table all these weeks, and I didn't know you. My eyes have been going for years, and I had been told that boy was dead, and whenever my heart said otherwise I told it to hush.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Four signs in a ring, the same as the ones carved on this stick of mine. I have leaned on it for ten years and never told a soul why.
after: Four signs in a ring, the same as the ones carved on this stick of mine. The Queen gave it to me the day I began teaching you, and I have leaned on it for ten years and never told a soul why.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: And my laboratory, my life's work, was used on that boy. It was used on you. Forgive me, if you ever can. I would understand it if you couldn't.
after: And my study, my life's work, was the thing they used on that boy. It was used on you, and I ran, and I never once asked who was behind those bars. Forgive me, if you ever can. I would understand it if you couldn't.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: You built the glass, Maren. You also gave me a bed and a pie when you still thought I might be a spy. I know which of those I'm keeping.
after: You ran, Maren. You also gave me a bed and a pie when you still thought I might be a spy. I know which of those I'm keeping.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: I knew as well. The Warden opens that tunnel for one family only, and I knew who you were the moment you came out of it. I was simply too frightened to say so.
after: I should have known you myself. I taught you your letters. But my eyes have been going for years, and I had been told that boy was dead, and I was too frightened to hope I'd been told wrong.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: So hear it from somebody who held your hand at court: you are {prince_full}, and I am so very sorry for what was done to you with the things I built.
after: So hear it from somebody who held your hand at court: you are {prince_full}, and I am so very sorry for what was done to you with the things I wrote.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: I knew whose daughter she was the day she sent you through my cave. Her father worked in my laboratory once, and I held that against her for far too long. I was wrong to do it.
after: I knew whose daughter she was the day she sent you through my cave. Her father was the best student I ever had, and I held what he became against her for far too long. I was wrong to do it.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Back where she came from, I expect: somewhere with glass walls and no windows. That's one door I can't open for you, dearie. Not yet.
after: Back where she came from, I expect: somewhere with bars on the doors and no windows. That's one door I can't open for you, dearie. Not yet.

speaker: (narration)
before: The oldest notes, at the far end, are in a different hand: careful, rounded, familiar. 'Observation, Year 1. The child is not a specimen. He asks for his mother. I am leaving the lab. M.'
after: The oldest note, at the far end, is in a different hand: careful, rounded, familiar. 'Year 1. I am told the subject is a child, and that he asks for his mother. A child is not a specimen. I will not stay to see it. M.'
